parts.solutionMd:

$\begin{aligned}7 x + 19 & = & 180\end{aligned}$

> *Solve the equation*

> *First subtract 19 from each side*

$\begin{aligned}7 x & = & 180 - 19 \\ 7 x & = & 161\end{aligned}$

> *Then divide both sides by 7*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & 161 \div 7 \\ x & = & 23\end{aligned}$

$3\times23+46=115$

**[M1]**

> *Also calculate the size of angle BCD to see which is largest*

> *Co-interior angles sum to 180° so subtract angle CDA to get angle BCD*

$180 - \left(3 \times 23 + 10\right) = 101$

> *Therefore angle ABC is the largest*

**Final answer:** **115°**

**[A1]**

> *Use the elimination method to solve the simultaneous equations (the substitution method will also work)*

> *To use the elimination method, the coefficient of one variable must be the same in both equations*

> *Make the coefficient of *$y$* the same by multiplying the second equation by 4*

$\begin{aligned}5 x + y & = & 3 \left(\times 4\right)\end{aligned}$* *

$\begin{aligned}20 x + 4 y & = & 12 \\ 6 x + 4 y & = & 19\end{aligned}$

> *Subtract the second equation from the first equation to eliminate the *$y$* variable*

$\begin{aligned}20 x + 4 y & = & 12 - \\ 6 x + 4 y & = & 19\end{aligned}$

*___________*

$14x=-7$

**[M1]**

$6 \left(- 0 . 5\right) + 4 \left(5 . 5\right) = 19$

> *Calculate the left hand side to check if it equals 19*

$-3+22=19$

> *The substituted values equate to 19 so they work together and are therefore correct*

> *We know each corner of triangle A has moved the same amount horizontally and vertically to get to triangle B*

*f = 9 - 13*
